anchor_line: Our club reference sheet: exact meaning behind calculator displays.

goals: Locate a value using squared bounds.

slides.title: RN2 · audit three exact-value claims
columns:
A: “π = 3.14 exactly.”
B: “√2 is rational because my calculator displays 1.414213562.”
“√16 is irrational because it has a root sign.”
slides.caption: Correct every claim on your own RN2 record.

slides.title: Locate the numbers
items: Place −3, −1/2, 0, √2 and 2 on a number line.
Use 1.4² and 1.5² to bracket √2.

slides.title: Exact values that display alike
items: Compare 1/3 with 0.333333333 as written.
Find two exact numbers that round to 1.41 at 2 decimal places.

slides.title: What changes when equality becomes approximation?
columns:
π ≈ 3.14
A finite √2 display is approximate.
slides.caption: A short display does not determine an underlying exact number’s class.

slides.title: Use squares to bracket the value
slides.caption: 1.4² = 1.96 and 1.5² = 2.25, so 1.4 < √2 < 1.5.

slides.title: Same rounded display, different exact values
slides.caption: 1.411 and 1.414 both round to 1.41. The number line locates √2; it does not prove irrationality.

5.preparation: RN5 record per learner; teacher-approved scientific calculators for roots, shared fairly if needed. Each learner records an actual entry. If unavailable, retain paper work and schedule an accessible device station.
5.route: Use the source’s actual-device route where supplied. Printed calculations do not certify device use. Mark missing/unobserved device work honestly.
